Relevant Resources

  • The new Hotpatching feature is now generally available. Please see Hotpatching feature for Windows Server Azure Edition virtual machines (VMs) for more information.
  • Windows 10 and Windows 11 updates are cumulative. The monthly security release includes all security fixes for vulnerabilities that affect Windows 10 and Windows 11, in addition to non-security updates. The updates are available via the Microsoft Update Catalog. For information on lifecycle and support dates for Windows 10 and Windows 11 operating systems, please see Windows Lifecycle Facts Sheet.
  • Microsoft is improving Windows Release Notes. For more information, please see What's next for Windows release notes.
  • A list of the latest servicing stack updates for each operating system can be found in ADV990001. This list will be updated whenever a new servicing stack update is released. It is important to install the latest servicing stack update.
  • In addition to security changes for the vulnerabilities, updates include defense-in-depth updates to help improve security-related features.
  • Customers running Windows Server 2008 R2, or Windows Server 2008 need to purchase the Extended Security Update to continue receiving security updates. See 4522133 for more information.

Title.Value: HEIF Image Extensions Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Use after free in HEIF Image Extensions allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to have a deep understanding of the system. Successful exploitation is not guaranteed and depends on a combination of factors that might include the environment, system configuration, and the presence of additional security measures.

Description.Value: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

Title.Value: Windows NTFS Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists when reparse points are created by sandboxed processes allowing sandbox escape. An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could use the sandbox escape to elevate privileges on an affected system.

To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker would first have to log on to the system, and then run a specially crafted application to take control over the affected system.

The security update addresses the vulnerability by preventing sandboxed processes from creating reparse points targeting inaccessible files.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

Description.Value: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

Title.Value: Windows Modern Device Management (MDM) Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Inadequate encryption strength in Windows Modern Device Management (MDM) allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

The attacker must inject themselves into the logical network path between the target and the resource requested by the victim to read or modify network communications. This is called a machine-in-the-middle (MITM) attack.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value: How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability? An attacker in a position to modify an affected device’s MDM network traffic could provide a specially crafted signed management response. Successful exploitation could allow code to run as SYSTEM. User interaction is not required.

Description.Value: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

Title.Value: Azure CycleCloud Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Improper neutralization of special elements used in an os command ('os command injection') in Azure CycleCloud allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain ROOT privileges.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value: How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability? An authenticated attacker who controls a compute node in an affected cluster could register a specially crafted node name. If an administrator later runs the affected topology operation, successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute commands as root on the cluster controller.

CWE.Value: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

Title.Value: Visual Studio Code Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Improper restriction of rendered ui layers or frames in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature locally.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
What security feature could be bypassed by successfully exploiting this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could bypass the Visual Studio Code Workspace Trust feature, allowing content from an untrusted workspace to run commands or code without the user first granting trust. See Workspace Trust for more information.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could convince a user to open a specially crafted Visual Studio Code workspace. Successful exploitation could bypass Workspace Trust protections and allow attacker-controlled content to execute code in the context of the user. User interaction is required, but the user does not need to grant trust.

CWE.Value: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

Title.Value: Windows CNG Key Isolation Service Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists when the Windows Cryptography Next Generation (CNG) Key Isolation service improperly handles memory. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could run processes in an elevated context.

To exploit this vulnerability, an attacker would first have to gain execution on the victim system. An attacker could then run a specially crafted application to elevate privileges.

The security update addresses the vulnerability by correcting how the Windows CNG Key Isolation Service handles memory.

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

Title.Value: Windows Advanced Rasterization Platform Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Advanced Rasterization Platform allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker who can run a malicious application locally inside an AppContainer could submit specially crafted graphics data to the isolated graphics compilation service. Successful exploitation could let the attacker perform actions within the affected service's isolated security context, outside the attacker's AppContainer. No action by another user is required.

Title.Value: Windows Kernel Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the way that the Windows Kernel handles objects in memory. An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could execute code with elevated permissions.

To exploit the vulnerability, a locally authenticated attacker could run a specially crafted application.

The security update addresses the vulnerability by ensuring the Windows Kernel properly handles objects in memory.

Title.Value: Windows Installer Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the Windows Installer when the Windows Installer fails to properly sanitize input leading to an insecure library loading behavior.

A locally authenticated attacker could run arbitrary code with elevated system privileges. An attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights.

The security update addresses the vulnerability by correcting the input sanitization error to preclude unintended elevation.

Notes.Title: Description

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is local (AV:L). Why does the CVE title indicate that this is a remote code execution?

The word Remote in the title refers to the location of the attacker. This type of exploit is sometimes referred to as Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE). The attack itself is carried out locally. This means an attacker or victim needs to execute code from the local machine to exploit the vulnerability.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
According to the CVSS metric, user interaction is required (UI:R). What interaction would the user have to do?

An attacker must send a user a malicious Office file and convince them to open it.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

Title.Value: Microsoft SQL Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Execution with unnecessary privileges in SQL Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
I am running SQL Server on my system. What action do I need to take?

Update your relevant version of SQL Server using the applicable November 2026 security update listed below.

There are GDR and/or CU (Cumulative Update) updates offered for my version of SQL Server. How do I know which update to use?

  • First, determine your SQL Server version number. For more information, see Microsoft Knowledge Base Article 321185 - How to determine the version, edition, and update level of SQL Server and its components.
  • Second, locate the range containing your current version number in the following table. The corresponding update is the one you need to install.

Note: If your version is not represented in the table, review the applicable update's prerequisites and the support status of your SQL Server release before choosing an update. Absence from this table alone does not establish that a version is unsupported.

What are the GDR and CU update designations and how do they differ?

General Distribution Release (GDR) updates provide security and other broadly applicable critical fixes. Cumulative Updates (CUs) include accumulated fixes for the applicable SQL Server release. Use the version ranges above to select the security update for your installed servicing branch; CU+GDR updates apply to the listed CU branch, while RTM+GDR updates apply to the listed RTM/GDR branch.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker who controls a replication peer could supply specially crafted data over an existing replication connection. Processing that data could allow code execution in the affected replication process. The attacker does not need an account on the target server, and no additional user interaction is required during normal replication.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
Why is the attack complexity rated High?

Successful exploitation requires the affected SQL Server instance to have the vulnerable replication feature and topology configured. An attacker with access to a participating database or replication peer cannot enable this server configuration through the vulnerability.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with permission to synchronize a database subscription could send a specially crafted request to an affected SQL Server instance. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute database commands beyond the intended replication functionality. No user interaction is required.

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Concurrent execution using shared resource with improper synchronization ('race condition') in Windows Point-to-Point Protocol over Ethernet (PPPoE) allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

Notes.Value: This CVE was assigned by Chrome. Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) ingests Chromium, which addresses this vulnerability. Please see Google Chrome Releases for more information.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
Why is this Chrome CVE included in the Security Update Guide?

The vulnerability assigned to this CVE is in Chromium Open Source Software (OSS) which is consumed by Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). It is being documented in the Security Update Guide to announce that the latest version of Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) is no longer vulnerable.

How can I see the version of the browser?

  1. In your Microsoft Edge browser, click on the 3 dots (...) on the very right-hand side of the window
  2. Click on Help and Feedback
  3. Click on About Microsoft Edge

Notes.Value: This CVE was assigned by Chrome. Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) ingests Chromium, which addresses this vulnerability. Please see Google Chrome Releases for more information.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
Why is this Chrome CVE included in the Security Update Guide?

The vulnerability assigned to this CVE is in Chromium Open Source Software (OSS) which is consumed by Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). It is being documented in the Security Update Guide to announce that the latest version of Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) is no longer vulnerable.

How can I see the version of the browser?

  1. In your Microsoft Edge browser, click on the 3 dots (...) on the very right-hand side of the window
  2. Click on Help and Feedback
  3. Click on About Microsoft Edge

Notes.Value: This CVE was assigned by Chrome. Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) ingests Chromium, which addresses this vulnerability. Please see Google Chrome Releases for more information.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
Why is this Chrome CVE included in the Security Update Guide?

The vulnerability assigned to this CVE is in Chromium Open Source Software (OSS) which is consumed by Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). It is being documented in the Security Update Guide to announce that the latest version of Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) is no longer vulnerable.

How can I see the version of the browser?

  1. In your Microsoft Edge browser, click on the 3 dots (...) on the very right-hand side of the window
  2. Click on Help and Feedback
  3. Click on About Microsoft Edge

Title.Value: Visual Studio Code Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Incomplete list of disallowed inputs in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
What security feature could be bypassed by successfully exploiting this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation could allow an extension to be installed and run despite an administrator's extension allowlist policy. The user must be convinced to install the extension.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
Why is the attack complexity rated High?

Successful exploitation through the extension marketplace requires the attacker to control a publishing identity that meets specific conditions. Obtaining that identity is a prerequisite beyond simply creating a malicious extension.

Title.Value: Visual Studio Code Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

A remote attacker could convince a user to open a specially crafted extension's details page in Visual Studio Code and select a malicious link. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code in the context of the user without installing the extension. The attacker does not need privileges on the user's system.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation depends on specific conditions in the user's Visual Studio Code environment, including an already-open integrated terminal. The attacker must also rely on the user viewing the affected extension's details page in a particular platform-compatibility state.

CWE.Value: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

Title.Value: Windows NTLM Spoofing Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor in Windows NTLM allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
According to the CVSS metrics, successful exploitation of this vulnerability could lead to major loss of confidentiality (C:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

This vulnerability discloses a user's NTLMv2 hash to the attacker who could use this to authenticate as the user.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

External attackers could send specially crafted emails that will cause a connection from the victim to an untrusted location of attackers' control. This will leak the Net-NTLMv2 hash of the victim to the untrusted network which an attacker can then relay to another service and authenticate as the victim.

Title.Value: Windows Kerberos Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Weak authentication in Windows Kerberos allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker who controls authentication in a trusted forest could send specially crafted authentication information to the target forest. Successful exploitation could raise the integrity level of the attacker's identity to System, allowing actions otherwise blocked by integrity-level restrictions where existing resource permissions already allow access. This does not grant SYSTEM-account privileges or target-forest administrator membership.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires an existing trust relationship between the attacker's forest and the target forest, together with resource permissions that already allow the attacker's identity access. The vulnerability bypasses integrity-level restrictions but does not grant otherwise absent resource access permissions.

Notes.Value: Improper restriction of xml external entity reference in Microsoft Dynamics 365 (on-premises) allows an authorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

The type of information that could be disclosed if an attacker successfully exploited this vulnerability is unauthorized file system access - reading from the file system.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
According to the CVSS metric, privileges required is low (PR:L). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Any authenticated attacker could trigger this vulnerability. It does not require admin or other elevated privileges.

CWE.Value: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

Title.Value: Microsoft Office Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could convince a user to view a folder containing a specially crafted file. The user does not need to open the file, and the attacker does not need an account on the affected system. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code with the permissions of that user.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

Title.Value: Windows Security Account Manager Remote Protocol Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Time-of-check time-of-use (toctou) race condition in Windows Security Account Manager allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

An unauthenticated attacker with network access to an affected domain controller could bypass account-lockout protections and make additional password-guessing attempts. Successful exploitation does not itself disclose a user's password.

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Improper privilege management in Microsoft Azure Kubernetes Service allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
What action do customers need to take to address this vulnerability?

Customers must upgrade the node images for affected Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) node pools to a node image containing the security update. Title.Value: Windows PowerShell Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Improper control of generation of code ('code injection') in Windows PowerShell allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could convince a victim, or cause a victim-controlled automated process, to invoke Invoke-WebRequest against an attacker-controlled URL. By returning a specially crafted non-2xx HTML response, the attacker could cause Windows PowerShell to parse the response through MSHTML without displaying the security confirmation prompt, which could execute embedded script in the invoking PowerShell process.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is local (AV:L). Why does the CVE title indicate that this is a remote code execution?

The word Remote in the title refers to the location of the attacker. This type of exploit is sometimes referred to as Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE). The attack itself is carried out locally.

For example, when the score indicates that the Attack Vector is Local and User Interaction is Required, this could describe an exploit in which an attacker, through social engineering, convinces a victim to download and open a specially crafted file from a website which leads to a local attack on their computer.

CWE.Value: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

Title.Value: Windows Function Discovery Resource Publication Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Use after free in Windows Function Discovery Resource Publication allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over an adjacent network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker on the same network segment could send specially crafted SOAP requests to a system running the Function Discovery Resource Publication service. Exploitation depends on inducing a low-memory allocation failure and winning an asynchronous request-cleanup timing condition. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code as SYSTEM.

Notes.Value:

Successful exploitation requires the target system to be under sustained low-memory (memory pressure) conditions, which are not commonly present in normal operation. This makes the vulnerability difficult to reliably trigger, as the attacker must first induce or wait for a constrained memory state before exploitation becomes possible.

Notes.Value: Origin validation error in Microsoft Teams for Android allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
According to the CVSS metrics, successful exploitation of this vulnerability could lead to major loss of confidentiality (C:H), but lead to no loss of integrity (I:N) or availability (A:N). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Title.Value: JDBC Driver for SQL Server Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Improper verification of cryptographic signature in JDBC Driver for SQL Server allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker who controls or can impersonate the SQL Server could replay a legitimate attestation response while substituting attacker-controlled key material during a client connection. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to obtain column encryption keys and access or modify protected database data.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires Always Encrypted with secure enclaves to use HGS attestation. The attacker must also control or impersonate the SQL Server connection and have access to a legitimate attestation response that can be replayed.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
What could an attacker accomplish by exploiting this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to bypass secure-enclave attestation, obtain column encryption keys, decrypt protected database data, and create modified encrypted data that the client accepts as valid.

Title.Value: Microsoft Office SharePoint Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to act with the SharePoint farm service identity's administrative privileges.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with permissions to add or modify content on an affected SharePoint page could store malicious script content in the page. The script could run in the security context of another user when that user views and interacts with the affected content, potentially allowing the attacker to access or modify SharePoint data available to that user.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

CWE.Value: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

Title.Value: Microsoft SQL Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Exposed dangerous method or function in SQL Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SQL sysadmin privileges.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
Why is the attack complexity rated High?

Successful exploitation requires the affected SQL Server instance to be configured as a replication distributor. Systems without this configuration are not affected.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
I am running SQL Server on my system. What action do I need to take?

Update your relevant version of SQL Server using the applicable November 2026 security update listed below.

There are GDR and/or CU (Cumulative Update) updates offered for my version of SQL Server. How do I know which update to use?

  • First, determine your SQL Server version number. For more information, see Microsoft Knowledge Base Article 321185 - How to determine the version, edition, and update level of SQL Server and its components.
  • Second, locate the range containing your current version number in the following table. The corresponding update is the one you need to install.

Note: If your version is not represented in the table, review the applicable update's prerequisites and the support status of your SQL Server release before choosing an update. Absence from this table alone does not establish that a version is unsupported.

Update Number Title Version Apply if current product version is… This security update also includes servicing releases up through…

5132748 SQL Server 2025 RTM+GDR (November GDR 2026) 17.0.1155.3 17.0.1000.7 - 17.0.1145.4 KB5128492 - Previous SQL2025 RTM GDR

What are the GDR and CU update designations and how do they differ?

General Distribution Release (GDR) updates provide security and other broadly applicable critical fixes. Cumulative Updates (CUs) include accumulated fixes for the applicable SQL Server release. Use the version ranges above to select the security update for your installed servicing branch; CU+GDR updates apply to the listed CU branch, while RTM+GDR updates apply to the listed RTM/GDR branch.

Title.Value: SQL Server Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Heap-based buffer overflow in SQL Server allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with low-level access to an affected server could send a specially crafted request to execute code on the server. User interaction is not required.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
I am running SQL Server on my system. What action do I need to take?

Update your relevant version of SQL Server using the applicable November 2026 security update listed below.

There are GDR and/or CU (Cumulative Update) updates offered for my version of SQL Server. How do I know which update to use?

  • First, determine your SQL Server version number. For more information, see Microsoft Knowledge Base Article 321185 - How to determine the version, edition, and update level of SQL Server and its components.
  • Second, locate the range containing your current version number in the following table. The corresponding update is the one you need to install.

Note: If your version is not represented in the table, review the applicable update's prerequisites and the support status of your SQL Server release before choosing an update. Absence from this table alone does not establish that a version is unsupported.

Update Number Title Version Apply if current product version is… This security update also includes servicing releases up through…
5129299 SQL Server 2025 CU10+GDR (November GDR 2026) 17.0.5045.3 17.0.4006.2 - 17.0.5035.5 KB5125471 - SQL2025 RTM CU10
5132748 SQL Server 2025 RTM+GDR (November GDR 2026) 17.0.1155.3 17.0.1000.7 - 17.0.1145.4 KB5128492 - Previous SQL2025 RTM GDR
5129300 SQL Server 2022 CU27+GDR2 (November GDR 2026) 16.0.4315.2 16.0.4003.1 - 16.0.4305.5 KB5126934 - SQL2022 RTM CU27 GDR
5132747 SQL Server 2022 RTM+GDR (November GDR 2026) 16.0.1220.3 16.0.1000.6 - 16.0.1210.3 KB5128493 - Previous SQL2022 RTM GDR
5132745 SQL Server 2019 CU32+GDR (November GDR 2026) 15.0.4510.2 15.0.4003.23 - 15.0.4500.2 KB5128494 - Previous SQL2019 RTM CU32 GDR
5132751 SQL Server 2019 RTM+GDR (November GDR 2026) 15.0.2210.4 15.0.2000.5 - 15.0.2200.2 KB5128495 - Previous SQL2019 RTM GDR
5132746 SQL Server 2017 CU31+GDR (November GDR 2026) 14.0.3570.2 14.0.3006.16 - 14.0.3560.2 KB5128496 - Previous SQL2017 RTM CU31 GDR
5132749 SQL Server 2017 RTM+GDR (November GDR 2026) 14.0.2150.2 14.0.1000.169 - 14.0.2140.2 KB5128497 - Previous SQL2017 RTM GDR

What are the GDR and CU update designations and how do they differ?

General Distribution Release (GDR) updates provide security and other broadly applicable critical fixes. Cumulative Updates (CUs) include accumulated fixes for the applicable SQL Server release. Use the version ranges above to select the security update for your installed servicing branch; CU+GDR updates apply to the listed CU branch, while RTM+GDR updates apply to the listed RTM/GDR branch.
